chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Al-Khalil ibn Hashim wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a man who heard the call to prayer and the call for suhoor (pre-dawn meal) during the month of Ramadan, so he assumed the call was for suhoor; he had intercourse and then exited, only to find that dawn had broken. He (peace be upon him) wrote in his own hand: 'He should make up that day, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone has intercourse during Ramadan thinking it is still night for suhoor?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the ruling for a man who mistakenly engaged in intercourse believing the call was for Suhoor, ruling that he only needs to perform Qada (make-up) rather than Kaffarah (expiation). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that major expiation is required for breaking the fast intentionally during daylight hours, whereas error or specific conditions may warrant only a make-up day. The Imam’s handwritten response underscores the precision of Imami fiqh in distinguishing between intent and action in ritual purity and fasting.
